questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Hungary?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Hungary article.

questions.proof: Budapest is the country's capital and largest city, and the dominant cultural and economic centre.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Hungary?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Hungary on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Hungary article.

questions.proof: It is bordered by Slovakia to the North, Ukraine to the Northeast, Romania to the East and southeast, Serbia to the South, Croatia and Slovenia to the Southwest, and Austria to the west.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Hungary?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Hungary article.

questions.proof: Hungarian is the official language, and is among the few in Europe outside the Indo-European family.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “After the fall of Nazi _____, Soviet troops occupied all of the country.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Nazi”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Hungary article, under the heading “Communist Hungary, 1946-1989”.

questions.proof: After the fall of Nazi Germany, Soviet troops occupied all of the country.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The greatest of them is Matthias Corvinus, famous for taking Austrian terrirories like _____, etc. and protecting the country against Ottoman aggression.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “terrirories”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Hungary article, under the heading “Medieval Hungary, 896-1526”.

questions.proof: The greatest of them is Matthias Corvinus, famous for taking Austrian terrirories like Vienna, etc. and protecting the country against Ottoman aggression.
